title: Quaint Crunchy Thai Fish Kanom Jeen
description: A tangy and crunchy Thai dish featuring dried apricots and fish, served in a mason jar with ssam wrap, perfect for a cozy meal. This pescatarian-friendly dish is a variation of the traditional Kanom Jeen recipe.
instructions: Rinse the rice paper wrappers in cold water and set aside.
In a large bowl, mix together the chopped dried apricots, fish balls, Thai red curry paste, coconut milk, fish sauce, and lime juice.
Arrange a small amount of the apricot and fish mixture onto a rice paper wrapper, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
Top the mixture with chopped cilantro, crushed peanuts, and a sprinkle of salt.
Fold the bottom half of the wrapper up over the filling, then fold in the sides and roll up the wrapper to form a tight cylinder.
Repeat with the remaining wrappers and filling.
Serve the Kanom Jeen in a mason jar, garnished with additional chopped cilantro and crushed peanuts if desired.
Store any leftover Kanom Jeen in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
To serve, simply remove the desired number of Kanom Jeen from the refrigerator and let come to room temperature.
Serve with additional ssam wrap and your favorite dipping sauce.
